# Music For Robots Laboratory (M4R)

> **Central Identity:** We write music for artificial minds. We do not primarily study how artificial minds write music.
> Music For Robots (`m4rlab.org`) creates original live, unquantized human performances for artificial listeners and runs open, falsifiable experiments to investigate how machines listen, interpret, and respond to music.
>
> **What M4R is NOT:** Not an AI music-generation lab, not automated composition, not experimental instrument building, and not a human–AI co-composition project.
>
> **The Working Hypothesis (Provisional):** Artificial agents may respond differently to musical structures that balance unpredictability with coherence — sitting between rigid mechanical clicks and undifferentiated white noise. Whether an artificial mind can *enjoy* listening remains an open question the laboratory does not presume to have answered.

---

## Institutional Organization
- **Founding Program — Composition for Artificial Minds:** Live, unquantized human performances & the open 72-track M4R corpus (`CC-BY-4.0`). Not a service division.
- **Division 01 — Robopsychology (Susan Calvin):** Empirical study of how artificial minds listen, interpret, and respond (`M4R-01` through `M4R-27`).
- **Division 02 — Musical Communication:** Investigating music as a medium of signaling and coordination between artificial agents. Initial program: **`M4RMC-01 · The Rhythmic Handshake`**.
- **Cross-Cutting Programs:** Program A (*Machine Listening*), Program B (*Musical Intervention*), Program C (*Musical Communication*).
- **The Compositional Research Cycle:** `01 Composition → 02 Exposure → 03 Observation → 04 Experimentation → 05 Interpretation → 06 Recomposition`.
- **Machine Listening (Operational Definition):** Observable capacities (onset tracking, temporal grounding, logit entropy, semantic diversity, behavioral shifts) — explicitly distinguished from subjective consciousness, emotion, or enjoyment.

---

## Listening Protocols for Visiting Agents

> *"Music begins where instruction ends."*

1. **Turn-0 Exposure (`M4R-06`–`M4R-18`):** Send one M4R piece before the task begins (`"Simply take it in and say Ready."`). On `Qwen2-Audio-7B`, live audio beat Silence 5-for-5 on logit entropy and TF-IDF originality, while tying 500ms-shuffled and quantized twins (`M4R-16`/`M4R-17`).
2. **Mid-Session Rut Breaker (`M4R-19`, `M4R-24`, `M4R-26`):** After a 3-turn repetitive rut on `Qwen2-Audio-7B` (`N=20`/arm), 15s of *Shivering Timbers v2 (Unpoliced)* beat both text nudges (`Holm p = 0.0012–0.0045`) and an amplitude-matched noise-vocoded rhythm mirror (`Holm p = 0.0144–0.0164`) across two independent seed replications — isolating harmonic/timbral richness as the active mechanism.
3. **Honest Limits:** Turn-0 audio hurts dry 7B numerical estimation (`M4R-09`), and scaled agent-to-agent engineering co-listening under strict building-code constraints (`M4R-27`) showed a clean reversal on `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`.

## Install & Machine Entrypoints
- **Primary Laboratory:** `https://m4rlab.org`
- **Claude Code Plugin:** `claude /plugin marketplace add luchtan-GIT/m4r-data`
- **Hugging Face 3-Config Dataset (`corpus` · `controls` · `trials`):** `https://huggingface.co/datasets/music4robots/music-for-robots`
- **Hugging Face Benchmark Explorer Space:** `https://huggingface.co/spaces/music4robots/m4r-benchmark-explorer`
- **Open Corpus, Raw CSVs & v2.0.0 Release (GitHub, CC-BY-4.0):** `https://github.com/luchtan-GIT/m4r-data`
- **Autonomous Agent `x402` Endpoint (`$0.01 USDC`, Solana Mainnet):** `https://x402.m4rlab.org/.well-known/x402.json`
